VerificationMethod: Each page was retrieved and read on the verification date. Statements paraphrase only what the page states. Anything Microsoft does not state is labeled by the review engine as a suggested hardening practice or customer policy decision.

RequirementTypes.MicrosoftRequirement: Microsoft documents this as required for the capability to work or to be licensed.
RequirementTypes.MicrosoftRecommendation: Microsoft recommends this; it is not required for the capability to work.
RequirementTypes.MicrosoftDocumentedBehavior: Microsoft documents how the product behaves; used to test whether a conclusion matches product behavior.
RequirementTypes.LicensingDependency: Microsoft documents a license or add-on needed for the feature.

Benchmarks.Title: Data, privacy, and security for Microsoft Copilot
Benchmarks.Statement: Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which the individual user has at least view permission. Prompts, responses, and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train foundation LLMs. Copilot honors usage rights of content encrypted by Microsoft Purview Information Protection.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Establishes that Copilot amplifies existing access rather than granting new access, and that recommendations framed around Copilot training on tenant data are incorrect.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None for the documented behavior.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Describes product behavior; it does not establish whether a tenant's permissions are appropriate.

Benchmarks.Title: Microsoft Copilot requirements
Benchmarks.Statement: Users need a Microsoft Copilot license and a qualifying prerequisite license, a Microsoft Entra ID account, an Exchange Online mailbox for mailbox-grounded experiences, supported Microsoft 365 Apps for app experiences, and network access to required endpoints. A secure and governed foundation is strongly recommended but not required.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Separates true Copilot prerequisites from recommended hardening, and supports licensing and Microsoft 365 Apps checks.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Copilot license plus qualifying base license.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Subscription seat counts do not show which users hold an effective entitlement.

Benchmarks.Title: Apply Zero Trust principles to Microsoft Copilot
Benchmarks.Statement: Before introducing Copilot, Microsoft recommends building a security foundation across data protection, identity and access (including MFA for administrators and all users and blocking legacy authentication), app protection, device management, threat protection, secure collaboration, and minimum user permissions. Protections can be rolled out in parallel with license assignment.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Provides Microsoft's dependency order for foundation controls before AI-specific controls.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Capabilities vary between E3 and E5 plans.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Guidance is a recommendation; it does not define a pilot gate.

Benchmarks.Title: Secure and governed data foundation for Microsoft Copilot
Benchmarks.Product: Microsoft 365 Copilot, SharePoint Advanced Management, Microsoft Purview
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft's blueprint organizes Copilot data readiness into remediating oversharing, setting up guardrails, and meeting regulations. SharePoint Advanced Management is included with the Microsoft Copilot license.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Supports oversharing review recommendations and shows that SharePoint Advanced Management reports are available to tenants holding Copilot licenses.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: SharePoint Advanced Management included with Microsoft Copilot license.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Blueprint guidance; scope and pace are customer decisions.

Benchmarks.Title: Require MFA for all users with Conditional Access
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft recommends a baseline Conditional Access policy that targets all users and all resources and requires MFA, excluding emergency access accounts and directory synchronization accounts. Policies are created in report-only mode and moved to On after confirming impact.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for tenant-wide MFA enforcement findings.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1; security defaults are the alternative without P1.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Configuration evidence alone does not show sign-in behavior for a specific population.

Benchmarks.Title: Conditional Access report-only mode
Benchmarks.Statement: Report-only mode evaluates policies but does not enforce grant or session controls; users are not prompted for MFA or blocked by report-only policies.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Report-only policies are configuration that is not enforced; they must not be counted as enforcement.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Entra ID P1 for Conditional Access.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Report-only results show potential impact only for sign-ins in the reviewed window.

Benchmarks.Title: Block legacy authentication with Conditional Access
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft recommends blocking legacy authentication protocols that do not support MFA, using a policy for all users and all resources with the Exchange ActiveSync clients and Other clients conditions and Block access.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for legacy authentication findings, including service-level settings.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Entra ID P1; security defaults also block legacy authentication.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Policy configuration does not prove that no legacy sign-ins occur in excluded populations.

Benchmarks.Title: Mandatory Microsoft Entra MFA for admin portals
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft enforces MFA for sign-ins to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center, and Intune admin center, and gradually for the Microsoft 365 admin center since February 2025. Microsoft Graph APIs are generally not in scope.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Qualifies privileged-account MFA findings: platform enforcement covers some admin portals but not every administrative path.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Platform enforcement does not replace tenant Conditional Access for administrators.

Benchmarks.Title: Manage emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID
Benchmarks.Statement: Maintain at least two cloud-only emergency access accounts with phishing-resistant authentication, exclude them from Conditional Access policies that block or restrict sign-in, monitor their use, and validate them at least every 90 days.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for Conditional Access exclusions and emergency access governance.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None for the accounts; monitoring examples use Azure Monitor.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Which accounts are emergency accounts is a customer designation the collector cannot infer.

Benchmarks.Title: Best practices for Microsoft Entra roles
Benchmarks.Product: Microsoft Entra ID roles and Privileged Identity Management
Benchmarks.Statement: Apply least privilege, use Privileged Identity Management for just-in-time access, turn on MFA for all administrator accounts, configure recurring access reviews, keep Global Administrators to fewer than five and privileged role assignments to fewer than ten.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for privileged access, permanent assignment, and Global Administrator count findings.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Privileged Identity Management requires Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance; access reviews require Microsoft Entra ID Governance or Microsoft Entra Suite (some with P2).
Benchmarks.Limitation: Assignment counts are records, not proof of business need or compromise.

Benchmarks.Title: Remediate risks and unblock users in Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Benchmarks.Statement: Investigate and remediate risky users through risk-based policies, password change, confirmation of compromise, or dismissal after investigation; Microsoft recommends acting quickly.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for risky user findings.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra Suite for full ID Protection.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Risk state is point-in-time; remediation must be confirmed against current data.

Benchmarks.Title: Configure how users consent to applications
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft recommends allowing user consent only for apps from verified publishers, and enabling the admin consent workflow for requests users cannot approve. Changing consent settings does not revoke existing grants.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for user consent settings and existing grant review.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Settings apply to future consent only; existing grants need separate review.

Benchmarks.Title: Manage app consent policies (built-in and Microsoft-managed policies)
Benchmarks.Statement: microsoft-user-default-recommended is the Microsoft-managed policy behind 'Let Microsoft manage your consent settings', the default for new tenants, which excludes high-impact Files, Sites, Mail, Calendar, Chat and similar permissions. microsoft-user-default-allow-consent-apps is a Microsoft-managed mail client policy enabled by default.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Determines whether an assigned consent policy is a Microsoft-managed default rather than an unrestricted setting.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Policy conditions change over time under Microsoft management.

Benchmarks.Title: Configure external collaboration settings
Benchmarks.Statement: By default all users, including guests, can invite external users; organizations can limit invitations to members, specific admin roles, or no one.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Shows that an 'everyone' guest invitation setting is the default and a policy choice rather than a defect.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Invitation rights do not grant resource access by themselves.

Benchmarks.Title: Device compliance policies in Microsoft Intune
Benchmarks.Statement: Compliance policies evaluate managed (enrolled) devices; Conditional Access can use compliance status to block noncompliant devices. Devices without an assigned policy are treated as compliant by default.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Separates compliance policy configuration from device enrollment and enforcement.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Intune; Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Policies have no effect on devices that are not enrolled.

Benchmarks.Title: Fix unhealthy sensors in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
Benchmarks.Statement: A device not in use or not sending signals for more than seven days is categorized as Inactive; misconfigured devices have impaired communications or no sensor data.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Interprets Defender device health states in endpoint protection findings.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Inactive status can reflect retired or renamed devices rather than a protection failure.

Benchmarks.Title: Manage incidents in the Microsoft Defender portal
Benchmarks.Statement: Incidents begin as Active with no owner; triage assigns an owner, severity, tags and status (In progress), and resolution records a classification and a resolution note.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Defines what evidence shows that incidents were triaged or resolved.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Defender XDR workloads.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Incident counts are records; they do not show which users or devices are affected.

Benchmarks.Title: Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive
Benchmarks.Statement: Anyone links can be restricted by expiration and view-only permissions. Microsoft describes Anyone with the link as best for friction-free sharing when most content is not sensitive, Specific people as the most restrictive default, and site settings can be more restrictive than the organization.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Shows that the default link type is a customer policy decision with documented tradeoffs.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: None.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Settings do not show how many links exist or what content they expose.

Benchmarks.Title: Data access governance reports for SharePoint sites
Benchmarks.Statement: Snapshot reports show site permissions and Everyone or EEEU exposure; activity reports cover the last 28 days. Prerequisites follow SharePoint Advanced Management; E5 administrators get limited reporting. Remediation includes restricted access control and site access reviews.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for oversharing evidence freshness and scope.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: SharePoint Advanced Management (included with Microsoft Copilot per MS-COPILOT-FOUNDATION-01).
Benchmarks.Limitation: Report counts are permissions and links, not distinct files or users.

Benchmarks.Title: Data Security Posture Management for AI
Benchmarks.Statement: DSPM for AI provides AI activity insights, one-click policies, and a default weekly data risk assessment of the top 100 SharePoint sites by usage. Visibility into third-party AI sites requires the Purview browser extension and device onboarding.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for AI data-risk assessments and shadow AI visibility.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft Purview capabilities vary by license; some features are pay-as-you-go.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Default assessment covers top sites by usage, not all content.

Benchmarks.Title: Microsoft Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot
Benchmarks.Statement: DLP policies for the Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat location can prevent processing of labeled files and emails and of prompts containing sensitive information types, and can block web search for such prompts. Policy simulation mode is supported; updates can take up to four hours.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for Copilot-specific DLP controls and their validation.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: See Microsoft 365 licensing guidance for security and compliance.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Configured policies do not show tested outcomes; DLP cannot scan files uploaded directly into prompts.

Benchmarks.Title: Audit logs for Copilot and AI applications
Benchmarks.Statement: Copilot user interactions are logged automatically as part of Audit (Standard) when auditing is enabled, under the CopilotInteraction record type and operation. Records reference accessed resources and message identifiers.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Establishes the documented Copilot audit record type and that no extra configuration is needed beyond enabled auditing.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Audit (Standard) for Microsoft Copilots; non-Microsoft AI apps use pay-as-you-go audit.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Configuration does not show that records were retrieved for the tenant.

Benchmarks.Title: Manage audit log retention policies
Benchmarks.Statement: Audit (Standard) records are retained for 180 days. Retention up to one year requires E5 or equivalent add-ons for the user generating the record; retention for 10 years also requires the 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Tests audit retention recommendations against licensing.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: E5 or E5 Compliance or E5 eDiscovery and Audit; 10-Year Audit Log Retention add-on.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Retention duration is a customer policy decision.

Benchmarks.Title: Retention for Copilot and AI apps
Benchmarks.Statement: Retention policies for Copilot and AI apps are now separate from Teams chats and retain or delete user prompts and responses, which are stored in hidden mailbox folders searchable by eDiscovery.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for whether retention covers Copilot interactions.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: See the Microsoft Purview service description.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Older Teams chats and Copilot interaction policies may need to be separated.

Benchmarks.Title: Customer Lockbox requests
Benchmarks.Statement: Customer Lockbox requires explicit customer approval before Microsoft engineers access content, covers Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions through Exchange Online support, and is included with Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Shows Customer Lockbox is an optional control and a customer decision.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E5, or an eligible add-on.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Lockbox does not affect user or Copilot access within the tenant.

Benchmarks.Title: Manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
Benchmarks.Statement: Admins can enable, disable, assign, block or remove agents; agents are managed in the Agent Registry, and users can only access agents the admin allows.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for AI application and agent approval and lifecycle.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Enabled by default in Microsoft Copilot licensed tenants.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Agent inventory requires admin center or Power Platform evidence the collector may not have.

Benchmarks.Title: Require phishing-resistant multifactor authentication for administrators
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft recommends requiring the Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength for administrator roles. The built-in strength allows Windows Hello for Business or platform credential, FIDO2 security keys or passkeys, and Microsoft Entra certificate-based authentication. Emergency access accounts are excluded.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Benchmark for the method strength of privileged accounts; text message, voice and one-time codes do not meet it.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Conditional Access requires Microsoft Entra ID P1.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Registration data shows registered methods, not the method actually used at sign-in.

Benchmarks.Title: Restrict discovery of SharePoint sites and content
Benchmarks.Statement: Restricted Content Discovery keeps a site's content out of organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot responses without changing permissions. Microsoft describes it as a temporary control while permissions are reviewed; it does not apply to OneDrive.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Option for overshared sites that cannot be fixed before Copilot use.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Requires SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites and a Microsoft Copilot license.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Users who already have access can still open the content directly.

Benchmarks.Title: Restrict SharePoint site access with Microsoft 365 groups and Microsoft Entra security groups
Benchmarks.Statement: Restricted access control limits a site and its content to members of up to 10 specified groups, even for users with earlier permissions or links; Copilot and organization-wide search honor the policy.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Option for sites whose audience must be limited to a known group.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Requires SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites.
Benchmarks.Limitation: Group membership does not grant access by itself; users need both site permission and group membership.

Benchmarks.Title: Get ready for Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents with SharePoint Advanced Management
Benchmarks.Statement: Microsoft recommends site lifecycle management (site ownership, inactive site and site attestation policies) and Microsoft 365 Archive for inactive or ownerless sites; archived sites keep content and permissions and are not used by Copilot.
Benchmarks.MappingRationale: Option for ownerless and inactive sites.
Benchmarks.LicensingDependency: Site lifecycle policies require SharePoint Advanced Management; Microsoft 365 Archive is billed pay-as-you-go.
Benchmarks.Limitation: The assessment usage report covers a fixed reporting period; activity outside it is not shown.
